widgets.stem: Tap the point that represents the ordered pair $(3, -2)$.
widgets.instrument: Spec example {"target":[3,2]} — a coordinate grid (−5..5); the student taps one lattice point. Target coordinates must be whole numbers in −5..5.

reading_fields.target: [x, y], the point the question asks for

diagnostics.predicate_meaning: Plotted (y, x) — the pair read in the wrong order
diagnostics.misconception_label: Treating an ordered pair like a set, so order does not matter
diagnostics.misconception_description: The student thinks (a, b) and (b, a) are the same, as if the pair were just the set {a, b} with no order.

widgets.stem: Let $X=\{2, -1\}$ and $Y=\{4, 0\}$. Build $X\times Y$ by tapping every ordered pair it contains.
widgets.instrument: Spec example {"X":[1,2],"Y":[3,4,5]} — the student taps ordered pairs to build X×Y (decoys are added automatically). Small sets only: 2–3 numbers each, at most 4. Validator limits (parseMathWidget): X and Y are non-empty lists of numbers.

reading_fields.X: the set X as a list
reading_fields.Y: the set Y as a list

diagnostics.predicate_meaning: Built Y×X — the pairs are the right numbers in the wrong order
diagnostics.misconception_label: Treats X×Y and Y×X as the same set
diagnostics.misconception_description: The student assumes that swapping the two sets gives the same set of pairs, as if the order of the sets did not matter.

widgets.stem: Let $Y=\{4, 0\}$ and $Z=\{4, 5, -2\}$. Build $Y\times Z$ by tapping every ordered pair it contains.

widgets.stem: A relation from $X=\{-1, 1, 2\}$ to $Y=\{2, 4, 6\}$ is made of ordered pairs $(a, b)$ with $a \in X$ first and $b \in Y$ second. Tap every ordered pair that could belong to a relation from $X$ to $Y$ (all of $X \times Y$).
widgets.instrument: Spec example {"X":[1,2],"Y":[3,4,5]} — the student taps ordered pairs to build X×Y (decoys are added automatically). Small sets only: 2–3 numbers each, at most 4. Validator limits (parseMathWidget): X and Y are non-empty lists of numbers.

reading_fields.X: the set X as a list
reading_fields.Y: the set Y as a list

diagnostics.predicate_meaning: Built Y×X — the pairs are the right numbers in the wrong order
diagnostics.misconception_label: Writes the pairs from Y to X instead of from X to Y
diagnostics.misconception_description: The student writes each ordered pair with the book type first and the student second, or draws the arrows from the books back to the students.
